jobs.title: Director, GTM Operations Analytics and Insights
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

Analyzes complex business problems and issues using data from internal and external sources to provide insight to decision-makers. Identifies and interprets trends and patterns in datasets. Builds recommendations to improve business unit effectiveness. May develop methods for measuring effectiveness of business unit work. Defines or contributes to analytics strategy. Works to ensure global consistency in data and analytic methods. Works to make data available and increase employees' capability to interpret and use data and analytics tools effectively. May partner with other professionals to develop, assess, facilitate and/or lead programs and processes to support business objectives and strategy implementation.

Responsibilities

Sets the strategy and direction for GTM analytics, insights, and reporting, defining how the organization measures performance and where analytics investment delivers the greatest business impact. Serves as a strategic partner to senior executives and client groups across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, and IT — shaping the questions that matter, surfacing emerging business problems, and influencing decisions at the C-suite level. Equips leaders with the data, forecasting, and predictive and prescriptive insights they need to make critical business decisions, while owning the integrity and global consistency of the data definitions those decisions rest on. Leads, mentors, and scales a high-performing analytics team, evolving its capability from reporting to insight generation and raising data fluency across the business.

Analytics Strategy and Thought Leadership

Drives strategy and direction for analytics and analytics priorities, ensuring alignment with business needs and EDNA commitment
Brings value to each ask and drives strategy and forward-thinking analytics that would have a stronger business impact. Provides support and development for Analysts and Senior Analysts
Stays connected with developments in GTM analytics in external markets and suppliers

Client and Stakeholder Management

Builds relationships and partners with stakeholders (i.e. IT, Finance, senior executive business leaders) to understand requests, make recommendations, implement solutions, and influence decisions. Coaches client groups to present data and insights to business leaders for better adoption and use of insights
Consults with senior executives and external subject matter experts to unearth emerging business problems requiring instrumentation
Leads prioritisation of asks for support from EDNA teams

Data Definitions & Integrity

Drives evolution of current data definitions with key stakeholders (including global and regional functional leads, Finance, EDNA and other functions) for GTM owned measures
Proactively identifies key emerging business metrics needed to adapt to evolution of business and strategy
Coordinates with the MDM and business to fix identified data integrity and inconsistency issues, recommending and implementing areas of improvement

Reporting, Analytics and Insights : Evolution and Development

Ensures delivery maintenance and optimization of key recurring CRO reporting, leveraging available DIO technology to optimise efficacy for recipients in line with their use case for the data
Delivers analytical insights on business performance, identify key trends and inputs for regular and ad-hoc deliverables
Leads activities to proactively build insights from highly complex multiple analytics platforms and data mining exercises to make recommendations to optimise business outcomes. This should include advanced predictive and prescriptive analytics

Team Leadership and Development:

Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Identify training and development needs to enhance team capabilities and ensure alignment with strategic goals
Build and evolve skills mix in team over time from reporting to insights capabilities

Qualifications

Consolidated experience in analytics, GTM/revenue operations, or BI, including senior leadership experience
Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or equivalent preferred
Track record leading and scaling an analytics function — team, process, and tooling
Deep knowledge of Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success data and how it drives revenue
Hands-on fluency with BI/data tools (SQL, Tableau, Power BI) and CRM platforms
Experience building forecasting models and predictive/prescriptive analytics for executives
Executive-grade communication; track record influencing C-suite/E-staff audiences

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance Operations & Transformation
jobs.description:
About Kinaxis

Are you looking to join an innovative, market-leading company where you can truly elevate your career? At Kinaxis we are serious about culture, we are serious about technology, we are serious about customers, and we are serious about not taking ourselves too seriously. If you are looking to be part of an incredible growth story, then we might just be the place for you!

In 1984, we started out as a team of three engineers. Today, we have grown to become a global organization with over 2000 employees around the world, 6 global office and a best-in-class HQ in Ottawa, Canada. As winners of several Top Employer awards globally, we are proud to work with our customers and employees towards solving some of the biggest challenges facing supply chains today.

Kinaxis is a global leader in modern supply chain orchestration, powering complex global supply chains, and supporting the people who manage them. Our powerful, AI infused platform provides full transparency and visibility across end-to-end supply chains, enabling our customers to make faster, better decisions. We are trusted by renowned global brands to provide the agility and predictability needed to navigate today’s volatility and disruption. With more than 40,000 users in over 100 countries, we are expanding our team as we continue to innovate and revolutionize how we support our customers.

Location

Our headquarters and most of our team are based in Ottawa. For employees located in Ottawa,

this role follows a hybrid work model, with an expectation of approximately four days per week

in the office at our headquarters. We also welcome remote candidates from anywhere in Canada

About The Team

The Vice President, Finance Operations & Transformation is a senior finance executive responsible for leading and scaling a modern finance operations team for a public company.

This leader owns the operational backbone of Finance: accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll operations, procurement, deal desk governance, customer contracting, and finance operations transformation.

The mandate is not simply to run today’s processes; it is to redesign and modernize them so the company can scale efficiently, improve the employee and customer experience, strengthen financial discipline, and operate with greater speed, consistency, automation, and insight.

The successful candidate will bring a transformation mindset and a strong operating cadence. They will be equally comfortable improving day-to-day execution, creating enterprise-wide standards, partnering with Sales and Legal on complex commercial transactions, working with IT on systems and workflow automation, and leading change across the finance organization.

Vacancy Status

This is an existing job vacancy

What you will do

Lead global finance operations across accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll operations, procurement, customer contracting and deal desk governance.
Ensure the efficient and accurate processing of all financial transactions, application of internal controls, and compliance with company policies and procedures.
Lead the team and serve as a global advisor on deal structuring, pricing strategy, and commercial terms to optimize revenue outcomes. Provide strategic insights into deal dependencies, risks, and opportunities to support global planning and execution.
Lead the transformation of finance operations by improving processes, leveraging technology, and introducing automation and AI where they create business value.
Identify opportunities to simplify, automate, or eliminate manual processes across financial operations.
Grow teams, develop leaders across the portfolio, and create an environment that supports collaboration, operational excellence, and modern enterprise thinking

What we are looking for

15 years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Significant experience with finance operations, finance transformation, procurement operations, or related environments.
Knowledge of industry best practices and emerging trends in finance transformation.
Proven ability to modernize processes through standardization, automation, analytics, AI-enabled tools, and operating model redesign.
Strong leadership skills to provide vision and support to the Finance team, mentor individuals, and develop high-performing talent.

#VP

#DF-LI1

Work With Impact:
Our platform directly helps companies power the world’s supply chains. We see the results of what we do out in the world every day, when we see store shelves stocked, when medications are available for our loved ones, and so much more.

Work with Fortune 500 Brands:
Companies across industries trust us to help them take control of their integrated business planning and digital supply chain. Some of our customers include Lockheed Martin, Unilever, P&G, ExxonMobil, Cisco and more.

Social Responsibility at Kinaxis:
Our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Committee weighs in on hiring practices, talent assessment training materials, and mandatory training on unconscious bias and inclusion fundamentals. Sustainability is key to what we do and we’re committed to a long-term net-zero operations strategy. We are involved in our communities and support causes where we can make the most impact.

People matter at Kinaxis and here are some of the perks and benefits we offer, which may vary by location and employee:

Flexible vacation and Kinaxis Days (company-wide days off)
Flexible work options
Physical and mental well-being programs
Regularly scheduled virtual fitness classes
Mentorship programs, training, and career development
Recognition programs and referral rewards
Hackathons

For more information, visit the Kinaxis website at www.kinaxis.com or the company’s blog at http://blog.kinaxis.com .

We provide accommodations upon request to ensure fairness and accessibility throughout our recruitment process for all candidates, including those with specific needs or disabilities. If you require an accommodation, please reach out to us at recruitmentprograms@kinaxis.com. This contact information is for accessibility requests only and cannot be used to inquire about the status of applications.

jobs.title: Director, Insights, Innovation and R&D (18-month Contract)
jobs.description:
The Director, Insights, Innovation, & R&D leads the consumer insight, menu innovation, product development, and food quality agenda for KFC Canada. This role turns consumer and business insight into a growth-driving innovation pipeline, modernizes KFC's core products, and leads the FIT (Food Innovation & Technology aka Product Development) team from concept through commercialization. The Director partners closely with Marketing, Operations, Supply Chain and franchisees to ensure products are distinctive, consumer-led, operationally executable and delivered to KFC quality and food safety standards. If you are a leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, can navigate ambiguity with action, has ambition to deliver impact and a spirit of what is possible – KFC is an environment that will empower and support your success.

Own the integrated consumer insights, menu strategy and innovation agenda, translating consumer, category and cultural insight into clear growth opportunities and the short-, medium- and long-term pipeline and business.
Lead the FIT team and end-to-end product development process, from culinary/product brief and prototyping through consumer validation, restaurant testing, commercialization and launch.
Modernize and continuously improve KFC Canada's core food portfolio, protecting what consumers love while improving taste, quality, consistency, value and relevance.
Build and deliver a differentiated innovation pipeline that supports the Marketing growth calendar, creates newsworthy reasons to choose KFC and strengthens the brand across priority occasions and consumer groups.
Act as guardian of KFC Canada's food philosophy and architect of the menu vision, defining the principles, product standards and strategic choices that guide product development and renovation.
Lead consumer insights across internal resources and agency partners, ensuring customer understanding is embedded in brand strategy, calendar development, innovation, value and broader business planning.
Set clear innovation learning agendas and stage gates; use consumer, operational and commercial evidence to make fast decisions on what to advance, optimize or stop.
Partner with Brand, Retail Marketing, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance and franchisees to ensure innovation is commercially compelling, operationally executable, scalable and supported by strong launch plans.
Own R&D prioritization, resources and ways of working, ensuring the team balances core product improvement, calendar innovation, longer-term pipeline development and rapid test-and-learn opportunities.
Provide leadership oversight of Quality Assurance within the team remit, ensuring robust product and supplier standards, food safety and quality systems, issue escalation, and continuous improvement in partnership with Operations and Supply Chain.
Deliver credible thought leadership and compelling recommendations to KFC Canada LT, franchisees and cross-functional stakeholders, aligning the system behind bold but evidence-based growth choices.
Build a high-performing, connected Insights, Innovation, R&D and QA capability with clear accountability, strong talent development and effective collaboration across the broader business.

Education/Certifications

Required: Post-secondary degree in business, marketing, or related discipline
Preferred: MBA

Experience

10+ years of progressive experience across consumer insights, innovation, product development/R&D, brand, food science or related commercial functions
Demonstrated experience leading teams and an end-to-end food innovation pipeline from insight and concept through product development, testing, commercialization and launch
Style that inspires and unites cross-functional teams, bringing clarity in strategy and empowering whilst holding accountable with a spirit of taking people with you.
Compelling communications capability, translating complex ideas simply to bring clarity and alignment across a diverse set of stakeholders.
Strong track record of translating consumer insight into commercial growth strategies and high-impact innovation.
Strong understanding of operations, supply chain and commercialization requirements; able to balance consumer desirability, operational feasibility and commercial viability.
Proven ability to modernize core products while building a forward-looking innovation pipeline.
Ability to influence senior leaders, franchisees, and complex matrixed stakeholders through ambiguity and transformation.
Ability to effectively develop and lead high-performing technical and commercial talent.
Ability to balance enterprise-level strategic thinking with curiosity, creativity, pace, and hands-on problem solving.
A passion for food, consumers, and emerging trends

We’d prefer this role to have…

Prior experience in QSR, food manufacturing/FMCG, or food retail

What makes KFC a great place to work?

Our People.
We invest in people capability above all else, with a proven track record of developing internal talent to leadership levels across the business both in Canada and globally. We hire and develop people who lead with Smart, Heart and Courage to make a big impact on the business today and grow into leaders of the future.

Our Culture.
We are known for a culture that rewards and recognizes bold results and promises everyone a seat at our table. We focus on your personal development as much as your professional development to ensure you can bring your best self to work.

Why you’ll love working here

Hybrid work model (2-3 days per week in office)
Paid vacation and personal days, plus 10 paid KFC Canada holidays in addition to statutory holidays.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits, including HSA and PSA options that allow you to personalize your coverage, plus life insurance and disability coverage, with employer-paid premiums
Family-inclusive Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and virtual care
Paid parental leave with salary top-up
RRSP and DPSP retirement programs with employer matching
Annual tuition reimbursement program
Employee referral rewards
And so much more!

Note: remuneration, benefits, and other perks may vary by role, employment status, eligibility, and other relevant factors.

jobs.description:
Req Id:

Connection is everything. It drives us to innovate, explore, and stay close to what matters to us most. At Bell, we’re building a more connected future through world-class networks, AI-powered solutions, and digital experiences that elevate how people live, work, and play every day.

We believe in empowering people. That’s why we equip our teams with cutting-edge technology, AI tools, and a collaborative environment that supports creativity and growth. Want to be part of a diverse team where your work makes a real impact? If you’re inspired by innovation that advances how people connect and transforms what’s possible, you belong on #TeamBell.

On the Bell Business Markets team, you’ll be a vital part of making innovation happen for enterprise-scale customers. You’ll deliver advanced solutions in areas such as IoT, Mobility/5G, Cloud, Cyber Security, Voice, Collaboration & Contact Centre and Internet & Private Networks.

At Bell, your skills and expertise will help set us apart as we continue to be the leading provider of digital connections and next generation services to businesses and governments.

Summary

Bell's AI Fabric initiative is building Canada's largest sovereign AI infrastructure platform, comprising seven large-scale, high-density data centres across the country, including a 500 MW British Columbia supercluster and a future 1.2 GW flagship campus in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Reporting to the VP, Capital Programs, the Director, Engineering & Procurement is responsible for providing leadership across engineering governance, technical strategy, strategic sourcing, procurement, and supplier management for Bell's national AI Fabric portfolio. This role will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams while overseeing the procurement of mission-critical infrastructure, ensuring Bell secures and delivers the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, network, and modular systems required to support hyperscale AI operations. Working closely with Construction, Program Controls, Commissioning, Operations, Finance, Legal, and external partners, the Director will drive engineering excellence, commercial value, supply chain resilience, and successful project execution across a multi-billion-dollar capital program.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the engineering and procurement functions supporting Bell AI Fabric developments across multiple Canadian sites.
Establish engineering standards, technical specifications, design governance processes, and quality assurance frameworks for mission-critical infrastructure.
Oversee engineering reviews and approvals for power distribution, utility interconnections, backup generation, UPS systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, controls, and related systems.
Develop and execute procurement strategies for major capital equipment, engineering services, and long-lead infrastructure components required for AI data centre development.
Lead supplier selection, commercial negotiations, contract management, and strategic partnerships with OEMs, engineering firms, utilities, EPC contractors, and technology vendors.
Drive capacity planning, infrastructure resiliency, technology roadmaps, and technical risk mitigation strategies supporting high-density AI and GPU workloads.
Partner with Construction, Commissioning, Operations, and Program Controls teams to ensure engineering and procurement activities align with project schedules, budgets, and operational requirements.
Manage supply chain risks, supplier performance, cost optimization initiatives, and procurement governance across the portfolio.
Provide executive-level recommendations regarding infrastructure investments, commercial strategies, engineering risks, and project delivery performance.
Develop and lead a high-performing team while fostering a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Critical Qualifications

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in engineering, procurement, construction, mission-critical facilities, data centres, energy infrastructure, or large-scale capital programs.
5+ years of people leadership experience managing engineering, procurement, project delivery, or integrated infrastructure teams.
Demonstrated experience delivering hyperscale data centres, mission-critical facilities, utility infrastructure, or large-scale industrial construction projects.
Strong technical expertise in electrical distribution systems, cooling infrastructure, liquid cooling technologies, resiliency design, and mission-critical operations.
Proven success leading strategic sourcing initiatives, complex commercial negotiations, and major procurement programs.
Deep understanding of engineering governance, capital project delivery, EPC contracting models, procurement practices, and commissioning processes.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, business case development, and contract administration.
Exceptional stakeholder management, communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Construction Engineering, or a related technical discipline; P.Eng. designation strongly preferred.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and travel as required to support projects across Canada.

Adequate knowledge of French is required for positions in Quebec.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Director, IT Cybersecurity to join our dynamic IT team. Lead the management and evolution of our cybersecurity policy, standards, runbooks and methodologies.

Measurable improvements in mean time to detect and respond to cybersecurity events.

A forward-looking, innovative, and adaptable mindset with the ability to anticipate organizational needs.
Demonstrated curiosity and commitment to lifelong learning; actively exploring new ideas, asking questions, and seeking knowledge to fuel innovation.

Demonstrated strengths in negotiation, budgeting, planning, organizing, and delegation.
Experienced in partnering with senior leaders to shape and deliver strategies that drive measurable results.

Ensure accounting processes scale effectively as the business grows in complexity across geographies, products, commercial models, and regulatory obligations.
Grow high-performing teams and create an environment that supports collaboration, operational excellence, and modern enterprise thinking.

15 years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Significant experience with public-company reporting, external audit, internal controls,

regulatory compliance, and Audit Committee support.

TSX experience is required; NASDAQ and NYSE experience is highly desirable.
Deep knowledge of IFRS, US GAAP, SOX, and internal control frameworks is highly

desirable, including direct experience owning SOX/ICFR programs.

Strong understanding of revenue recognition (IFRS 15/ASC 606) and operational finance

best practices.

Big Four public accounting background, particularly with public-company audit, SEC/OSC

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Every transaction matters. Every Canadian matters. At Interac, we protect both — driving trust, security, and inclusion, so our digital economy thrives.

Founded in 1984, Interac connects Canadians through secure digital payments, advanced identity verification and industry-leading fraud protection. Connecting banks, businesses, and individuals, Interac enables millions to send, receive, and manage money safely and effortlessly every day — across both digital and physical environments.

As the backbone of Canada’s financial ecosystem, Interac facilitates over 20 million transactions daily, supported by trusted partnerships with government and financial institutions. Consistently ranked as Canada’s most reputable financial technology brand, Interac is deeply embedded in the daily lives of Canadians.

Who You Will Work With:

About The Role

The Vice President, Financial Accounting & Reporting is a senior accounting and controllership executive for a global public company. Working in close partnership with the CFO, the VP, Financial Accounting & Reporting ensures the integrity, discipline, and operational effectiveness of the company’s financial management framework across accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, audit oversight, compliance, and revenue accounting globally.

The role serves as a trusted advisor to the CFO and Audit Committee on financial governance, controllership, regulatory readiness, and enterprise risk management related to financial operations and reporting

What you will do

Lead the day-to-day operating rhythm of the accounting, external reporting, and internal control functions, with accountability for efficient and accurate close processes, disciplined financial administration, and effective oversight of core accounting operations and global compliance.
Ensure timely, accurate, and decision-useful financial reporting, including external reporting obligations such as OSC and SEC filings and public disclosures, in compliance with IFRS/US GAAP, internal policies, and public-company requirements.
Oversee audit readiness, external audit coordination, control certification support, Canada NI 52-109 requirements, U.S. Sarbanes-Oxley readiness, and the operational processes required to maintain a strong compliance posture across jurisdictions.
Partner with risk management and internal audit.
Support the CFO in Audit Committee matters and serve as a senior operational counterpart on financial governance, controls, and compliance topics.
Ensure accounting processes scale effectively as the business grows in complexity across geographies, products, commercial models, and regulatory obligations.
Grow high-performing teams and create an environment that supports collaboration, operational excellence, and modern enterprise thinking.

What we are looking for

15 years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Significant experience with public-company reporting, external audit, internal controls,

regulatory compliance, and Audit Committee support.

TSX experience is required; NASDAQ and NYSE experience is highly desirable.
Deep knowledge of IFRS, US GAAP, SOX, and internal control frameworks is highly

desirable, including direct experience owning SOX/ICFR programs.

Strong understanding of revenue recognition (IFRS 15/ASC 606) and operational finance

best practices.

Big Four public accounting background, particularly with public-company audit, SEC/OSC
reporting, SOX/ICFR, or complex technology clients.

Strong presentation and communication skills at the senior management and board level
